lines.quote: I designed the digital beamforming architecture, including null-steering algorithms for interference rejection and the real-time calibration-update loop that keeps the beam patterns stable as the array's thermal environment changes.

Designed and implemented embedded DSP algorithms in C and C++ for Tuulikallio's radar signal processor product line, including real-time pulse compression and moving-target-indication filters running on Analog Devices SHARC ADSP-21489 hardware within sub-millisecond processing budgets.

RF characterisation of receive-chain components (LNAs, mixers, band-pass filters) using Rohde & Schwarz FSW spectrum analyser and ZVB vector network analyser setups in Tuulikallio's in-house RF laboratory. Maintained calibration procedures and measurement protocols for the lab's anechoic chamber.
S.M. Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Charles River Institute of Technology, 2002

Developed the signal-processing algorithms for an airborne maritime surveillance radar delivered to a Nordic defence customer, including clutter-suppression and target-detection modules adapted to the platform's motion-compensation requirements.

Co-authored three peer-reviewed conference papers on adaptive clutter-suppression techniques, presented at SESE Radar Conference (2009, 2014) and ISRT International Conference on Radar Systems (2017).
Danish citizen; EU/EEA freedom of movement applies. No work-permit requirements in Finland.

All technical documentation, design specifications, and customer-facing reports produced in English throughout my career at Tuulikallio. Regular technical coordination with partner organisations in the UK, Norway, and Denmark.
Willing to relocate to Oulu; currently based in Tampere.
I have already looked into the practicalities of a move to Oulu and the relocation would be straightforward -- my notice period at Tuulikallio is three months.
